newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-IAAF REDUCES DRUGS BAN TO TWO YEAR.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-IAAF REDUCES DRUGS BAN TO TWO YEAR.

text.p: The International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) halved its ban for serious drugs offences from four to two years on Thursday after a heated debate on the final day of its two-day congress.
Delegates voted 112-56 with three abstentions for a proposal from several European countries, headed by Germany, to cut the ban for first offenders,
The four-year ban, passed by the congress in 1991, has been regarded by some civil courts as too harsh and constituting restraint of trade.
On Thursday, IAAF president Primo Nebiolo, speaking in support of the resolution, said the world governing body had spent $1.7 million on fighting doping last year.
German Athletic Federation chief Helmut Diegel also spoke in favour.

The four-year ban was introduced when the sport was still recovering from the 1988 Ben Johnson scandal. The Canadian sprinter tested positive for steroids after winning the Seoul Olympic 100 metres final.
Two years ago in Gothenburg, the congress rejected a similar resolution after a heated debate when delegates argued successfully that a reduction would send the wrong signal to drugs cheats.
